Visible: Mr.9 OP14-095, Monkey.D.Luffy OP15-051, X.Drake OP10-114 (foil-looking), Yu EB03, Vasco Shot, plus a stack of sleeved cards.

Corrected the researcher's claim of $30 hammer listed 2026-09-13: that date was $180 (BOX OF POKEMON CARDS & EPHEMERA); the $30 results were 2025-09-28, 2025-11-10, 2026-03-23 and 2026-06-21. lots.guide_summary: Nothing same-item survives for the whole lot: Gowans has no past One Piece bulk box. Category guides only: 4 SOLD Gowans entries (Pokemon boxes mostly $20 to $90 hammer, anime card bulk $25 to $35, generic trading card boxes $40, graded One Piece singles $30 to $45), 0 unsold, 3 PriceCharting per-card guides showing visible cards at US$0.04 to US$3 each (rate 1 USD = 1.4328 AUD). Realistic value for this box is probably $20 to $50 hammer.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD evidence (no One Piece bulk sale found), so keep and flip maximums are 0. For reference only: if it behaved like an anime bulk box at $25 to $35 hammer, resale on a marketplace less about 13% fees and $10 to $15 postage would leave little after a /2.396 flip factor (e.g. ($40 x 0.87 - $12) / 2.396 = about $9). Visible singles are worth cents to a few dollars each.
lots.confidence_reason: Identification as One Piece is certain from the card faces, but only one photo shows the top of the box, the count is a guess, and there are no same-item sold results.
lots.key_photo_findings: Cards are One Piece Card Game, not Pokemon (Bandai layout, DON/counter text, set codes OP14-095, OP15-051, OP10-114, EB03-0xx). X.Drake OP10-114 has a foil sheen and textured border. A thick stack of sleeved cards (dark blue sleeves) at bottom, contents unseen. A few cards at lower left are partly hidden and could be another game. Light play wear visible.
lots.condition: Played or pack-fresh commons, light edge wear on some; box is a worn cardboard carton. Rest of contents unseen.
lots.question_for_gowans: The title says Pokemon but the visible cards are One Piece. Is there any Pokemon in the box, roughly how many cards in total, and what is in the sleeved stack at the bottom?

Title says only one is silver. No mark visible.

lots.guide_summary: No same-item or close entries survive. 6 SOLD Gowans category guides for small silver or animal-form boxes, $60 to $160 hammer; 0 unsold; 0 asking. Melt can't be worked out without a weight and purity. At silver about AUD 84.76/oz (about $2.72/g fine, a goldpricez figure another check recorded today, which I did not fetch again), a 50 g box at 800 fineness would melt at about $109, and an 80 g box at sterling about $200.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD evidence, so both maximums are 0. Reference only: the category guides cluster at $70 to $160 hammer for one small marked silver box, and the second (non-silver) bird would add perhaps $20 to $60. Weight and mark would decide value; ask Gowans before bidding.
lots.confidence_reason: No mark read, no weight, base not shown, and it's not stated which bird is silver. Evidence is category-guide only.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo, side view only. Both birds heavily repousse and chased with feather scales, the larger with glass or bead eyes and a flower spray, the smaller with a twisted collar. Both have a seam at mid-body (lift-off lids). Silvery grey toning on both, with no obvious brassing, so the photo can't tell which is silver. The lot ticket has older handwritten numbers in blue (struck through, '88' visible), suggesting a previous vendor or lot number. No hallmark visible.
lots.condition: Light tarnish, no visible dents or splits at this size; bases and interiors not seen.
lots.question_for_gowans: Which of the two birds is silver, is there any mark on the base or inside the lid (e.g. 800, 925, 'silver', country), what does each weigh, and do the lids fit and are there any dents or splits?
